## Lead Nurture Automation Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: A new listing in the CRM or MLS feed, a rate change from your lender's feed, an anniversary or birthday in the CRM, or a lead going quiet for N days each start a run for the leads they affect.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - No message without a reason the lead would recognise; the model cannot invent one.
   - Frequency cap: at most one touch per lead per 14 days, at most three per quarter.
   - Anyone in an active conversation or an active CRM stage is excluded automatically.
   - Unsubscribe and STOP are honoured on the first word; suppression is written to the CRM.
   - Fair-housing language check on every draft; flagged drafts cannot be sent.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/lead-nurture-automation/
Want it built and run for you? $197/month · custom $2,000–3,500 one-time

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger: Detect the reason
nodes.notes:
Detect the reason

Hourly: new listings, rate changes and CRM dates are compared against every lead's stated wants (area, beds, budget, timeline) and their history.

assignments.name: config.your_name
assignments.value: Your name — signs every outgoing message

assignments.name: config.approver
assignments.value: #approvals — a Slack channel, or an email address

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- CRM leads with wants and history (Follow Up Boss, kvCORE, HubSpot)
- Listing feed (CRM or MLS)
- Rate feed or manual rate table
- Agent voice samples
- Calendar for showings

nodes.name: Code: Match leads to the signal
nodes.notes:
Match leads to the signal

A listing matches a lead when area, price band and beds fit; a rate move matches leads whose budget was near the edge; an anniversary matches one person. No match, no message.

nodes.name: Code: Check the guardrails
nodes.notes:
Check the guardrails

Skip anyone contacted in the last 14 days, anyone who unsubscribed, anyone with an open conversation, and anyone whose CRM stage is 'active' — the agent is already talking to them.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Draft the message" step of the Lead Nurture Automation Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Two to four sentences in the agent's voice that name the reason, reference what the lead said last time, and ask one question. Fair-housing wordlist applied.

Rules:
- No message without a reason the lead would recognise; the model cannot invent one.
- Frequency cap: at most one touch per lead per 14 days, at most three per quarter.
- Anyone in an active conversation or an active CRM stage is excluded automatically.
- Unsubscribe and STOP are honoured on the first word; suppression is written to the CRM.
- Fair-housing language check on every draft; flagged drafts cannot be sent.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: AI Agent: Draft the message
nodes.notes:
Draft the message

Two to four sentences in the agent's voice that name the reason, reference what the lead said last time, and ask one question. Fair-housing wordlist applied.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Draft the message
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

nodes.name: Slack approval: Approve or auto-send
nodes.notes:
Approve or auto-send

For the first month every draft goes to the agent for a tap; afterwards, message types the agent has approved ten times run without review.

Send-and-wait: the run pauses here until someone presses Approve or Reject. Set config.approver in "Config (edit me)".

nodes.name: Approved?
nodes.notes: True = approved → continue to the write-back. False = rejected → stop here; the item stays where it was.

nodes.name: Rejected: Approve or auto-send
nodes.notes: Rejected by the approver. Nothing is written. Optionally log the rejection to your sheet so the weekly count of corrections is visible.

nodes.name: Gmail: Send and log
nodes.notes:
Send and log

Sent from the agent's own address, threaded where a thread exists; the CRM gets a note and the 'last touched' date.

nodes.name: Gmail Trigger: Stop on reply
nodes.notes:
Stop on reply

A reply ends the sequence for that person and forwards the thread to the agent with the lead's history in three lines.

nodes.name: Google Sheets: Report
nodes.notes:
Report

Monthly: touches sent by reason, replies, showings and listings that came from a nurture touch, so the agent sees what a reason is worth.
